purpose: Test whether unequal calendar duration plausibly explains cross-system lambda magnitudes by directly comparing the frozen constant segment-retention model with a monotone exponential calendar-time retention model.

segment_constant.equation: E_next = Z gamma + lambda E_current + error
segment_constant.role: reproduces the original segment-scale retention estimand

calendar_exponential.equation: E_next = Z gamma + exp(-k * delta_t_days) E_current + error
calendar_exponential.role: retrospective continuous-calendar-time sensitivity, not a new primary estimator

nuisance_specifications.rule: use the same nuisance structure as the frozen primary segment model
add standardized log(delta_t_days) as a nuisance term to both competing models so mean downstream phase may vary with interval duration

comparison.metric: Gaussian AIC difference with equal parameter counts, delta_AIC = n*log(SSE_exponential/SSE_segment)
comparison.classification_rule: both specifications >=2 => SEGMENT_RETENTION_PREFERRED; both <=-2 => CALENDAR_DURATION_DECAY_SUPPORTED; otherwise SPECIFICATION_SENSITIVE_OR_INCONCLUSIVE

scientific_limits: This diagnostic is retrospective and cannot count as prospective support.
A monotone exponential model cannot represent negative lambda sign reversal; Svalbard is therefore a declared nonrepresentable boundary, not forced into k.
Failure of calendar-time exponential decay does not prove that duration never matters; it rejects this simple time-homogeneous retention model on the frozen design.
The interval-standardized k_eq remains descriptive even if calendar exponential decay is unsupported.
No result from this diagnostic may alter the preregistered Aikens fixed-24h contrast.
